topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning aims
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture’s place in the series and introduces its intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Mutation-driven clonal evolution and its epigenetic qualification
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop an account of tumor evolution through cell-intrinsic changes, then qualify mutation-driven selection by showing that epigenetic disruption can also cause transformation.

topics.label: Stemness, cell of origin and tumor-propagating hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how a cell’s position in a differentiation hierarchy influences its capacity to initiate or sustain cancer.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness in cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that allow previously non-transforming mutant cells to develop tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors’ dependence on supportive surrounding cells and the therapeutic opportunities created by that dependence.

topics.label: Single-cell and spatial methods for investigating cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how molecular profiling methods reveal tumor evolution and interactions between cells in human tissue.

topics.label: Interacting conditions for malignant evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This synthesis explains cancer susceptibility as the convergence of cellular properties and environmental conditions, extending that account to developmental contexts such as childhood cancer.

topics.label: Lecture close and next session
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces that the next session will address therapy.
